meta.title: Ontario G1 Prep — DriveTest Practice
meta.source: Official MTO Driver's Handbook (ontario.ca), checked against ontario.ca on 2026-11-06
meta.disclaimer: This handbook is only a guide. For official purposes, refer to the Highway Traffic Act, the Motorized Snow Vehicles Act and the Off-Road Vehicles Act of Ontario.
meta.g1_format: 40 questions: 20 Road Signs + 20 Rules of the Road. Pass = at least 16/20 (80%) in EACH section separately. Failing one section fails the whole test. G1 package fee $159.75 — confirm at drivetest.ca, fees change.
meta.warn_range_correction: CORRECTED 2026-11-06 — the handbook's warn-range figures (3 days first / 7 days second) are OUTDATED. Current penalties for BAC 0.05–0.079: 1st offence = 7-day suspension + $250 penalty + 8-hour alcohol education program; 2nd = 14-day suspension + $350 + 16-hour alcohol treatment program; 3rd = 30-day suspension + $450 + 16-hour treatment program + 6-month ignition interlock. BAC 0.08 or over, or refusing a sample: immediate 90-day administrative suspension (ADLS) + 7-day vehicle impoundment.

lessons.title: Defensive driving: visibility, space, communication (Intro)
learning_points: Defensive driving = see danger before it happens; based on visibility, space, communication.
Mirrors every ~5 seconds; look far ahead.
Cushion of space all round; greatest risk is in front.
Signal + eye contact; you can be found responsible even if the other driver was wrong.
Be predictable and courteous.
lessons.india_note: In India honking is routine and asserting right-of-way is normal. In Ontario the horn is only to get attention when needed, and you can be found at fault even if the other driver was wrong — yield if it avoids a collision.

questions.q: What are the three ideas defensive driving is based on?
questions.source: Intro, "Defensive driving is based on three ideas: visibility, space and communication."

questions.q: How often should you check your mirrors?
questions.source: Intro/Driving along, "checking your mirrors every five seconds or so."

questions.q: Where is the greatest risk of a collision?
questions.source: Intro, "the greatest risk of a collision is in front of you, stay well back."

questions.q: If another driver does something wrong and a collision happens, can you still be found responsible?
options: No, the wrong driver is always at fault
Yes, if you could have done something to avoid it
questions.source: Intro, "Even if someone else does something wrong, you may be found responsible for a collision if you could have done something to avoid it."

questions.q: What does courteous driving include?
options: Giving other drivers space to change lanes, not cutting them off, signalling properly
questions.source: Intro, courteous driving definition.

lessons.title: Getting ready to drive
learning_points: Don't drive sick, tired, upset, or on impairing medication.
Seating: see the ground 4 m ahead; headrest middle behind head.
Seatbelts: everyone, every trip; driver responsible for under-16s.
Child seats: <9 kg rear-facing; 9–18 kg child seat + tether; booster 18–36 kg, under 8, under 145 cm; seatbelt alone at 8 yrs / 36 kg / 145 cm.
Headlights: 150 m visibility, 110 m illumination, low beams within 150 m oncoming / 60 m behind, required ½ hr before sunset to ½ hr after sunrise and when you can't see <150 m.
lessons.india_note: In India children often ride unrestrained and rear seatbelts are rarely used. In Ontario every passenger, every trip, must be buckled — the driver is legally responsible for passengers under 16, with fines + demerit points.

questions.q: From the driver's seat you should be able to see the ground how far in front of the vehicle?
questions.source: L1, "see the ground four metres in front of the vehicle."

questions.q: A driver who does not buckle up can be fined and given how many demerit points?
questions.source: L1, "Drivers who do not buckle up can be fined and will be given two demerit points."

questions.q: An infant weighing less than 9 kg (20 lb) must be buckled into:
options: A forward- facing child car seat
questions.source: L1, "Infants who weigh less than 9 kilograms (20 lbs.) must be buckled into a rear-facing child car seat."

questions.q: A booster seat must be used by a child who is under 8, weighs 18–36 kg, and is less than:
questions.source: L1, booster-seat criteria "less than 145 centimetres (4 feet, 9 inches) tall."

questions.q: When must your headlights be on?
options: Between ½ hour before sunset and ½ hour after sunrise, and any time poor light keeps you from clearly seeing people/vehicles less than 150 m away
questions.source: L1, headlight requirement.

lessons.title: Driving along
learning_points: Hands at 9 and 3; steer smoothly, both hands on the wheel.
Signal well before every move; signalling alone is not enough.
Keep right except to pass or turn left.
Default speed limits 50 km/h in towns / 80 km/h elsewhere; 2-second following distance minimum.
Police directions override lights/signs; documents must be produced immediately, not within 24 hours.
lessons.india_note: India drives on the left, so 'keep right' and left turns across oncoming traffic feel reversed. Following distances under 1 second and horn-based driving are normal in India; Ontario tests the counted 2-second rule, and tailgating = 4 demerit points.

questions.q: Where should your hands be on the steering wheel?
questions.source: L2, "place your hands at nine o'clock and three o'clock."

questions.q: Where there is no posted speed limit, the maximum speed is:
options: 50 km/h in cities, towns and villages, and 80 km/h elsewhere
questions.source: L2, default speed limits.

questions.q: What is the minimum safe following distance in ideal conditions?
questions.source: L2, "A safe following distance is at least two seconds behind the vehicle in front of you."

questions.q: When a police officer directs traffic differently from a traffic light, you must:
options: Follow whichever is safer in your judgement
questions.source: L2, "you must follow their directions, even if the directions are different from traffic lights or signs."

questions.q: Cruise control should NOT be used:
options: In wet, icy or slippery conditions, heavy traffic, or when fatigued
questions.source: L2, cruise-control warning.

lessons.title: Sharing the road
learning_points: Yield to pedestrians in most cases; eye contact matters.
Pass cyclists with ≥1 m; failure = fine + 2 points.
School bus red lights: stop both directions (median excepted), ≥20 m from behind.
Trucks: blind spots, long stopping distance, wide turns — don't enter the gap.
Bus in a bay signalling left must be let back into traffic; farm machinery ≤40 km/h with orange-red slow-moving sign.
lessons.india_note: In India cyclists and pedestrians are expected to yield to cars. In Ontario the car yields — pass cyclists with at least 1 m (2 points if you fail), and stopping for a flashing-red school bus from both directions is one of the most tested G1 items.

questions.q: When passing a cyclist, a driver must maintain a minimum distance of:
questions.source: L3, "maintain a minimum distance of one metre, where practical."

questions.q: When a school bus has its overhead red lights flashing, a driver approaching from the rear must stop at least:
questions.source: L3, "stop at least 20 meters away."

questions.q: If you can't see a large truck driver's face in the truck's side-view mirror:
options: The truck is about to turn
The truck driver cannot see you
questions.source: L3, "if you can't see the driver's face in the large vehicle's side-view mirror, the driver cannot see you."

questions.q: When a bus in a bus bay flashes its left-turn signals to leave, a driver in the adjacent lane must:
options: Allow the bus to re-enter traffic
questions.source: L3, "you must allow the bus to re-enter traffic."

questions.q: Farm machinery on the road displays an orange and red slow-moving sign meaning it travels at:
questions.source: L3, "travelling at 40 km/h (Kilometres per hour) or less."

lessons.title: Driving through intersections
learning_points: Controlled vs uncontrolled intersections.
Blocked intersection: stop before entering (unless turning).
Uncontrolled, same time: left yields to right.
All-way stop: first to stop goes first; tie → left yields to right.
Turning always yields; signalling gives no right-of-way; yield to pedestrians until they COMPLETELY cross at crossovers/school crossings.
lessons.india_note: In India intersections are negotiated by size and horn, and blocking the box is routine. In Ontario strict first-arrival and right-hand rules apply at all-way stops and uncontrolled intersections, and entering a blocked intersection going straight is prohibited.

questions.q: At an uncontrolled intersection, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, who goes first?
questions.source: L4, "the driver on the left must let the driver on the right go first."

questions.q: At an intersection with stop signs at all corners, if two vehicles stop at the same time:
options: The vehicle on the left goes first
The vehicle on the right goes first / left yields to right
questions.source: L4, all-way-stop rule.

questions.q: You approach an intersection on a main road and it is blocked with traffic. You are going straight. You should:
options: Enter and wait in the intersection
Stop before entering and wait until traffic ahead moves on
questions.source: L4, blocked- intersection rule.

questions.q: When entering a road from a private road or driveway, you must yield to:
options: Vehicles on the road and pedestrians on the sidewalk
questions.source: L4, driveway-entry rule.

questions.q: Does signalling give you the right-of-way?
options: No — you must make sure the way is clear
questions.source: L4, "signalling does not give you the right-of-way."

lessons.title: Stopping
learning_points: Stop sequence: line → crosswalk → sidewalk edge → intersection edge.
Railway crossings: stop ≥5 m from the rail/gate; never go around a barrier; never stop on tracks; train can take 2 km to stop.
School bus: stop both directions, ≥20 m from behind, 6 demerit points for failing to stop.
School crossing guard: wait until everyone INCLUDING the guard clears the whole roadway; 3 points.
Pedestrian crossovers: yield until pedestrians completely cross; no passing within 30 m.
lessons.india_note: In India slowing at a stop sign often passes for stopping. In Ontario a complete stop at a precise place (line, then crosswalk, then sidewalk edge, then intersection edge) is a tested sequence.

questions.q: There is a stop sign but no stop line, no crosswalk and no sidewalk. Where do you stop?
options: In the middle of the intersection
At the edge of the intersection
questions.source: L5, stop-position sequence.

questions.q: If a train is coming at a railway crossing, you must stop at least how far from the nearest rail or gate?
questions.source: L5, "stop at least five metres from the nearest rail or gate."

questions.q: Failing to stop for a school bus with its red lights flashing carries how many demerit points for a first offence?
questions.source: L5, "six demerit points for a first offence."

questions.q: At a school crossing, when may you proceed?
options: When the guard lowers the sign
Only when all people, including the school crossing guard, have cleared the entire roadway
questions.source: L5, school-crossing rule.

questions.q: You must not pass any vehicle within how many metres of a pedestrian crossover?
questions.source: L5, "You must not pass any vehicle within 30 metres of a pedestrian crossover."

lessons.title: Changing directions
learning_points: Finish braking before turning the wheel; don't brake and steer at the same time.
Right on red after a full stop unless signed otherwise; left on red only one-way → one-way.
Waiting to turn left: keep wheels straight until you can complete the turn.
Roundabouts: circulating traffic has right-of-way; counter-clockwise; signal exit with right indicator after passing the exit before yours.
U-turn: 150 m visibility both ways; banned on curves, hilltops, near railway crossings, bridges/tunnels. Backing up: look over your shoulder; seatbelt may be removed while reversing.
lessons.india_note: Right turn on red after a full stop is legal in Ontario unless signed otherwise — there is no equivalent concept in India. Left on red is allowed only one-way to one-way. U-turns need 150 m visibility both ways.

questions.q: Unless a sign tells you not to, you may turn right on a red light:
options: Without stopping if the way is clear
Only after a complete stop and waiting until the way is clear
questions.source: L6, right-turn-on-red rule.

questions.q: You may turn left on a red light when:
options: Turning from a one-way road onto a one-way road, after a complete stop
questions.source: L6, left-turn-on-red rule.

questions.q: While stopped waiting to turn left, you should NOT turn your steering wheel to the left because:
options: Your vehicle could be pushed into oncoming traffic if hit from behind
questions.source: L6, "With your wheels turned to the left, your vehicle could be pushed into the path of oncoming traffic."

questions.q: In a roundabout, who has the right-of-way?
questions.source: L6, "Traffic in the roundabout has the right-of-way."

questions.q: You must never make a U-turn unless you can see at least how far in both directions?
questions.source: L6, "Never make a U-turn unless you can see at least 150 metres in both directions."

lessons.title: Changing positions
learning_points: Lane-change steps: mirrors → blind spot/shoulder check → signal → check again → steer gradually without slowing.
Return to your lane only when you see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your inside mirror.
Never pass a moving snow plow; never race a vehicle you are passing.
Shoulder: right shoulder only, to pass a left-turning vehicle, only if paved.
Pass streetcars on the right; stay ≥2 m behind rear doors at stops.
lessons.india_note: In India overtaking is from either side, often with the horn, and cutting back early is normal. In Ontario pass on the left and return only when you see the whole front of the passed vehicle in your inside mirror; never race a vehicle you are passing.

questions.q: What is the correct order for a lane change?
options: Check mirrors, check blind spot over shoulder, signal, check again, steer gradually
questions.source: L7, lane-change steps 1–4.

questions.q: After overtaking, when may you move back into your original lane?
options: When you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your inside mirror
When the other driver flashes lights
questions.source: L7, passing step 3.

questions.q: You may drive on the right shoulder only to:
options: Pass a vehicle turning left, and only if the shoulder is paved
questions.source: L7, passing-on-the-shoulder rule.

questions.q: You must pass streetcars on the:
options: Right, unless on a one-way road
questions.source: L7, "You must pass streetcars on the right unless you are driving on a one-way road."

questions.q: At a streetcar stop, stay at least how far behind the rear doors where passengers get on/off?
questions.source: L7, "stay at least two metres behind the rear doors."

lessons.title: Parking along roadways
learning_points: No-parking distances: 3 m hydrant, 9 m intersection (15 m if light-controlled), 15 m railway rail, 100 m bridge, 125 m clear view.
Dutch reach: open the driver's door with the right hand to force a shoulder check.
Parallel parking: space ~1.5× vehicle length; ~1 m from the car ahead.
Hill parking: downhill → wheels to curb; uphill with curb → wheels to road; uphill without curb → wheels sharply right.
Roadside stop: ≤30 cm from curb; hazards on.
lessons.india_note: Parking distances from hydrants, intersections and railways are not codified in Indian driver memory. Ontario tests 3 m / 9 m / 15 m / 100 m / 125 m, plus hill-parking wheel direction (downhill to curb, uphill with curb to road, uphill without curb sharply right).

questions.q: Do not park within how many metres of a fire hydrant?
questions.source: L8, "Do not park within three metres of a fire hydrant."

questions.q: Do not park within 9 m of an intersection, or within how many metres if it is controlled by traffic lights?
questions.source: L8, parking-distance rules.

questions.q: When parking facing downhill, turn your front wheels:
options: Towards the curb or right shoulder
questions.source: L8, "When parking facing downhill, turn your front wheels towards the curb or right shoulder."

questions.q: To parallel park, you need a space about how much longer than your vehicle?
questions.source: L8, "find a space that is about one and one-half times longer than your vehicle."

questions.q: The "Dutch reach" means opening the driver's door with your:
options: Right hand, forcing a shoulder check
questions.source: L8, Dutch reach description.

lessons.title: Freeway driving
learning_points: G1 drivers may drive on freeways only with a licensed driving instructor.
Enter via acceleration lane: match freeway speed BEFORE merging.
Look 15–20 seconds ahead; keep right, left lanes for passing.
Exiting: signal into the deceleration lane without slowing; beware velocitization (speed adaptation).
Missed exit: never stop/reverse — take the next exit. HOV: ≥2 people, open 24/7, never cross the striped buffer, large trucks banned.
lessons.india_note: India has no HOV lanes and missing an exit often means stopping or reversing. In Ontario match freeway speed in the acceleration lane before merging, and never stop or reverse on a freeway — take the next exit. G1 on a freeway only with a licensed instructor.

questions.q: A Class G1 driver may drive on a freeway only:
questions.source: L9, "Class G1 drivers may only drive on freeways with a licensed driving instructor."

questions.q: On a freeway, you should look ahead to where you will be in the next:
questions.source: L9, "Look ahead to where you are going to be in the next 15 to 20 seconds."

questions.q: If you miss your freeway exit, you should:
options: Stop on the shoulder and wait
questions.source: L9, "If you miss an exit, do not stop or reverse on the freeway. Take the next exit."

questions.q: What is "speed adaptation" (velocitization)?
options: Losing the ability to judge your speed accurately after driving at high freeway speed
questions.source: L9, "Losing your ability to judge your speed accurately is sometimes called speed adaptation or velocitization."

questions.q: Provincial HOV lanes are reserved for vehicles carrying at least:
questions.source: L9, HOV reserved for "vehicles carrying at least two people."

lessons.title: Dealing with particular situations
learning_points: Road rage: don't compete, retaliate, or "educate"; if followed, drive to a police station/busy public place, never home.
Drowsy driving: peak 2–6 a.m. and 2–4 p.m.; 8 warning signs; only cure is sleep.
Construction zones: doubled fines for speeding when workers present; don't change lanes.
Distracted driving: ~100 killed / 16,000 injured per year in Ontario; texting = 10× crash risk; handheld ban applies even stopped at a red light.
Emergency vehicles: stop immediately to the right curb (NOT the shoulder); move over + slow down for stopped emergency vehicles/tow trucks (3 points for failing to).
lessons.india_note: In India emergency vehicles are often not yielded to systematically and phone use stopped at a red light is common. In Ontario stop immediately to the right curb (not the shoulder), and the handheld ban applies even when stopped in traffic or at a red light.

questions.q: Drowsy-driving collisions most often occur:
questions.source: L10, drowsy-driving peak windows.

questions.q: If you believe you are being followed by an aggressive driver, you should:
options: Drive to a police station or a busy public place
questions.source: L10, threatened-driver instructions.

questions.q: About how many people are killed by distracted drivers every year in Ontario, according to the handbook?
questions.source: L10, "About 100 people are killed and 16,000 are injured by distracted drivers every year in Ontario."

questions.q: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights/siren, you must stop:
options: As near as practical to the right-hand curb or edge of the roadway
In the middle of the road
questions.source: L10, approaching-emergency-vehicle rule ("Do not move onto or stop on the shoulder").

questions.q: Fines for speeding in a construction zone when workers are present are:
questions.source: L10, "doubled fines for speeding in a construction zone when workers are present."

lessons.title: Driving at night and in bad weather
learning_points: Overdriving your headlights: stopping distance farther than you can see.
Fog/whiteout: LOW beams (never high beams), use the right edge as a guide, never stop on the travelled portion.
Hydroplaning: tires ride on water; slow down, good tread.
Skid: ease off, steer where you want to go; ABS pulsation is normal — don't release the pedal; threshold braking is for non-ABS cars, don't pump.
Black ice: shiny black asphalt, bridges/overpasses freeze first; snow plows: flashing blue lights visible 150 m, never pass between staggered plows.
lessons.india_note: Snow, ice, black ice, whiteouts and snow plows are new knowledge for an Indian driver. In fog and snow use LOW beams (never high beams) and never stop on the travelled portion; if stranded, stay with the vehicle.

questions.q: You are "overdriving your headlights" when:
options: Your stopping distance is farther than you can see with your headlights
questions.source: L11, overdriving definition.

questions.q: In fog, you should use:
questions.source: L11, "Use your low-beam headlights. High beams reflect off the moisture droplets in the fog."

questions.q: Hydroplaning happens when:
options: Your tires ride on top of water like water skis
questions.source: L11, hydroplaning definition.

questions.q: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:
options: Ease off the accelerator or brake and steer in the direction you want to go
Turn the wheel sharply opposite the skid
questions.source: L11, skid recovery.

questions.q: Snow-removal vehicles have flashing blue lights that can be seen from:
questions.source: L11, "flashing blue lights that can be seen from 150 metres."

lessons.title: Dealing with emergencies
learning_points: Brakes fail: pump the pedal, then parking brake gently but firmly holding the release button; don't drive away.
Gas pedal sticks: lift with foot, else hazards + neutral + stop off the road.
Freeway trouble: pull to the shoulder at the first sign; stay in the locked vehicle; don't raise the hood.
Wheels off pavement: foot off gas, no heavy braking, steer back when under control.
Collisions: report to police if injuries or damage >$5,000; under $5,000 exchange information but no police report needed; "Steer it, Clear it" for drivable no-injury collisions.
lessons.india_note: In India minor collisions are usually settled on the spot. In Ontario report to police when there are injuries or damage over $5,000, and failing to remain at the scene = 7 demerit points. Move drivable vehicles off the road first ('Steer it, Clear it').

questions.q: If your brakes fail, what should you try first?
questions.source: L12, "Try pumping the brake pedal to temporarily restore hydraulic brake pressure."

questions.q: If your gas pedal sticks and you cannot lift it with your foot, you should:
options: Turn on hazard lights, shift to neutral, stop as soon as safely possible off the road
Turn off the ignition while moving
questions.source: L12, stuck-gas-pedal procedure.

questions.q: If you have trouble on a freeway, you should:
options: Begin to pull over at the first sign of trouble, to the nearest shoulder
questions.source: L12, freeway-trouble procedure.

questions.q: By law, you must report a collision to the police when there are injuries or damage exceeding:
questions.source: L12, "$5,000" reporting threshold.

questions.q: If your wheels go off the pavement, you should:
options: Grip the wheel firmly, take your foot off the gas, avoid heavy braking, steer back when under control
Turn sharply back onto the pavement
questions.source: L12, wheels-off-pavement procedure.

lessons.title: Driving efficiently
learning_points: Turn off the vehicle if parked more than 10 seconds; engines warm up within 30 seconds.
A/C vs windows: windows/vents in the city, A/C at high speed.
Don't top off the tank.
Maintenance matters: worn spark plugs, dragging brakes, low transmission fluid, transmission not reaching high gear all raise fuel use.
The "10 ways" list (two-second space, blind spot, yield when in doubt, etc.) doubles as course revision.
lessons.india_note: Mostly universal eco-driving. The testable items are the numbers: turn the engine off if parked more than 10 seconds; engines warm up within 30 seconds.

questions.q: You should turn off your vehicle if parked for more than:
questions.source: L13, "Turn off your vehicle if parked more than 10 seconds."

questions.q: At high speeds, using your air conditioning is usually:
options: Less fuel efficient than opening windows
More fuel efficient than opening windows
questions.source: L13, A/C guidance.

questions.q: Which of these can increase fuel consumption substantially?
questions.source: L13, "Worn spark plugs, dragging brakes, low transmission fluid or a transmission not going into high gear can increase fuel consumption substantially."

questions.q: One of the handbook's "10 ways" to make Ontario's roads the safest is to keep at least:
questions.source: L13, "Keep at least a two-second space between your vehicle and the one ahead."

questions.q: You should NOT "top-off" the tank when refuelling because:
questions.source: L13, "Don't 'top-off' the tank when refueling. Spilled fuel releases harmful vapours."

lessons.title: Sign families: shape and colour
learning_points: Stop: 8-sided, red, white letters.
Yield: triangle, white, red border.
School zone: 5-sided, fluorescent yellow/green, black symbols.
Railway crossing: X-shaped, white, red outline.

Four families: regulatory (rect/square, white/black; green circle = may/must do, red circle+line = not allowed), warning (yellow diamond), temporary (orange diamond), information/ direction (green rectangle, white letters).
lessons.india_note: In India warning signs are mostly triangular (red border, white). In Ontario warning = yellow DIAMOND and temporary = orange DIAMOND — shape and colour are the first identification cue and are directly tested.

questions.q: A stop sign is:
questions.source: B1, stop-sign description.

questions.q: A yield sign is:
options: A triangle with a white background and red border
questions.source: B1, yield-sign description.

questions.q: Warning signs are usually:
questions.source: B1, warning-sign description.

questions.q: Temporary condition signs are usually:
questions.source: B1, temporary-condition-sign description.

questions.q: A sign with a red circle and a line through it means:
options: You may do the activity shown
The activity shown is not allowed
questions.source: B1, "A red circle with a line through it means the activity shown is not allowed."

lessons.title: Regulatory signs
learning_points: Green circle = may/must do; red circle+line = prohibited.
Do Not Stop / Do Not Stand / Do Not Park — three different meanings (not even a moment / except loading passengers / except loading passengers or merchandise).
Lane-use signs: lane 1 left, lane 2 left-or-straight, lane 3 right (example).
Community safety zone = increased fines.
School-zone speed limit applies when the yellow lights are flashing.
lessons.india_note: India has no 'green circle = may/must do; red circle with a line = prohibited' system. In Ontario this is a core regulatory-sign rule, and Do Not Stop / Do Not Stand / Do Not Park mean three different things.

questions.q: A sign with a green circle means you:
options: May or must do the activity shown inside the ring
questions.source: B1, regulatory-sign rule.

questions.q: "Do not stop" in the area between the signs means:
options: You may stop briefly to drop someone off
You may not stop your vehicle in this area, even for a moment
You may stop only at night
questions.source: B1, "Do not stop" definition.

questions.q: "Do not stand" in the area between the signs means you may not stop except:
questions.source: B1, "Do not stand" definition.

questions.q: In a community safety zone, traffic offences are subject to:
questions.source: B1, community-safety-zone sign.

questions.q: A school-zone speed limit sign means the lower speed limit applies:
options: Only when the yellow lights are flashing
questions.source: B1, "Observe the speed limit shown when the yellow lights are flashing."

lessons.title: Warning signs
learning_points: Advisory-speed tab under a curve warning = maximum safe speed for the curve.
Chevron groups guide drivers around sharp curves.
"Share the road" = provide safe space for cyclists and other vehicles.
Divided highway begins/ends — keep to the right-hand road.
Hidden school bus stop, deer crossing, railway crossing ahead (with track angle), truck/fire/bus entrances.
lessons.india_note: Warning signs are yellow diamonds in Ontario. Learn the advisory-speed tab (maximum safe speed for the curve) and chevron groups (guide you around sharp curves).

questions.q: A sign posted under a curve warning showing a number is:
options: The speed limit for the road
The maximum safe speed for the curve
questions.source: B1, "this sign shows the maximum safe speed for the curve."

questions.q: Chevron (arrowhead) signs posted in groups are used to:
questions.source: B1, chevron description.

questions.q: A "share the road" sign warns motorists to:
options: Drive in the centre of the road
Provide safe space on the road for cyclists and other vehicles
questions.source: B1, share-the-road description.

questions.q: "Divided highway begins" means:
options: Traffic travels in both directions on separated roads ahead; keep to the right-hand road
The road narrows to one lane
questions.source: B1, divided-highway-begins description.

questions.q: A warning sign showing a deer means:
options: Deer regularly cross this road; be alert for animals
questions.source: B1, deer-sign description.

lessons.title: Temporary, information/direction and other signs
learning_points: Temporary: construction 1 km ahead; doubling of HTA fines for speeding in a construction zone when workers are present; do not pass the pilot/pace vehicle.
Freeway exit numbers = distance from the start of the freeway (401 exit 204 = 204 km from Windsor).
Slow-moving vehicle: orange triangle, red border, ≤40 km/h.
LCV placard: double trailer up to 40 m.
EDR signs: emergency detour when OPP close a provincial highway.
lessons.india_note: In India exit numbers are sequential. In Ontario freeway exit numbers are distance-based — Highway 401 exit 204 is 204 km from Windsor. The slow-moving vehicle sign (orange triangle, red border) means 40 km/h or less.

questions.q: A temporary condition sign saying "Construction work one kilometre ahead" is what colour/shape?
questions.source: B1, temporary-condition signs are "usually diamond-shaped with an orange background."

questions.q: The sign enforcing doubled HTA fines applies to speeding in a designated construction zone when:
questions.source: B1, "Enforces doubling the HTA fines for speeding in a designated construction zone when there are workers present."

questions.q: Interchange number 204 on Highway 401 means it is how far from Windsor, where the freeway begins?
questions.source: B1, "interchange number 204 on Highway 401 is 204 kilometres from Windsor."

questions.source: B1, slow-moving-vehicle sign.

lessons.title: Traffic lights
learning_points: Green: go only after yielding to vehicles/pedestrians already in the intersection.
Yellow: stop if you can do so safely.
Red: full stop; right on red after stop unless signed otherwise; left on red only one-way → one-way.
Advance green / flashing green: oncoming traffic still red; pedestrians must not cross on it.
Flashing red = complete stop; flashing yellow = proceed with caution; blank lights = treat as all-way stop, yield to the right; transit priority = white vertical bar, yield to transit.
lessons.india_note: Flashing green / advance green and fully protected left-turn arrow phases do not exist in the same form in India. A dead traffic light is treated as an all-way stop in Ontario — yield to the right.

questions.q: A yellow (amber) light means:
options: Speed up to beat the red
The red light is about to appear; stop if you can do so safely, otherwise go with caution
questions.source: B2, yellow-light rule.

questions.q: When you face a flashing green light (advance green), it means:
options: You may turn left, go straight or turn right; oncoming traffic still faces a red light
questions.source: B2, advance-green rule.

questions.q: A flashing red light means:
options: Come to a complete stop; move through only when safe
The light is broken — treat as green
Stop only if traffic is coming
questions.source: B2, flashing-red rule.

questions.q: During a power loss, traffic lights are blank. You should:
options: Treat the intersection like an all-way stop, yielding to vehicles in the intersection and to vehicles entering from your right
questions.source: B2, blank-traffic-lights rule.

questions.q: A transit priority signal shows:
options: A white vertical bar on a dark background
questions.source: B2, "shows a white vertical bar on a dark background."

lessons.title: Pedestrian signals and pavement markings
learning_points: Walk = white walking symbol; hand (flashing or steady orange) = do not BEGIN to cross; pedestrians already crossing keep right-of-way and should hurry to a safe area.
No pedestrian signal + green light: pedestrians may cross; never on a flashing green or left-turn arrow.
Yellow lines = opposite directions; white lines = same direction.
Solid line left = unsafe to pass; broken line left = may pass if clear.
Continuity lines on the left = your lane is ending/exiting. Crossover markings: double white lines + X in each approaching lane; stop before the line until pedestrians completely cross.
lessons.india_note: In India lane markings are often ignored or faded. In Ontario solid vs broken, yellow vs white, and continuity lines are explicit pass / no-pass rules and are tested.

questions.q: A flashing or steady orange hand symbol means pedestrians:
options: Have the right-of-way to start crossing
Should wait for a green light
questions.source: B3, "A flashing or steady orange hand symbol means pedestrians must not begin to cross."

questions.q: Pedestrians who have already begun crossing when the hand signal appears should:
options: Go as quickly as possible to a safe area; they still have the right-of- way over vehicles
questions.source: B3, hand-signal rule.

questions.q: Yellow pavement lines separate:
options: Traffic travelling in the same direction
questions.source: B4, "Yellow lines separate traffic travelling in opposite directions."

questions.q: A solid line at the left of your lane means:
questions.source: B4, "A solid line at the left of your lane means it is unsafe to pass."

questions.q: Continuity lines on your left generally mean:
options: The lane you are in is ending or exiting and you must change lanes to continue
questions.source: B4, continuity-lines rule.

lessons.title: Getting your licence / Graduated Licensing
learning_points: GLS: G1 (12 months; 8 with approved course) → G2 (≥12 months) → G; at least 20 months total; two road tests.

G1 rules: zero BAC; accompanied driver (front seat only, Class G+, ≥4 years' experience, BAC <0.05%); no 400-series highways posted over 80 km/h (QEW, DVP, Gardiner, E.C. Row, Conestoga Parkway); no midnight–5 a.m.

New residents: 60 days on a foreign licence; India is non-reciprocating — max 12 months' credit, experience within past 3 years, authentication letter within 6 months; ≥12 months' experience → G2 road test immediately, then ≥12 months to G test.
G2 under-19 passenger limits midnight–5 a.m.: 1 passenger ≤19 in first 6 months, up to 3 after.
Test logistics: arrive 30 min early; 10 days between road tests; <48-hour cancellation = fee lost; out-of-order test loses 50% of the fee.
lessons.india_note: India has no graduated licensing. Ontario: G1 (12 months, 8 with an approved course) to G2 (at least 12 months) to G — minimum 20 months. India is non-reciprocating: no licence exchange, maximum 12 months' foreign experience credit.

questions.q: How long does Level One (G1) last, and how long with an approved driver-education course?
questions.source: C1, "Level One lasts 12 months… If you pass an approved course, you can complete Level One in eight months."

questions.q: A G1 driver's accompanying driver must have at least how many years of driving experience?
questions.source: C1, "at least four years of driving experience."

questions.q: A G1 driver must not drive on 400-series highways with a posted speed limit over:
questions.source: C1, G1 highway restriction.

questions.q: A new Ontario resident may use a valid foreign driver's licence for:
questions.source: C1, "you can use that licence for 60 days in Ontario."

questions.q: Applicants from non-reciprocating jurisdictions (such as India) can claim a maximum of how many months of foreign driving experience?
questions.source: C1, "can claim a maximum of 12 months of driving experience."

lessons.title: Keeping your licence / demerit points
learning_points: Points stay on your record 2 years from the offence date.
Novice: warning letters at 2 and 6 points; suspension at 9+ points for 60 days; points then reduced to 4; second time = 6 months.
Fully licensed: warnings at 6 and 9; suspension at 15 points for 30 days; points then reduced to 7; second time = 6 months.

Table highlights: 7 points — failing to remain at a collision, failing to stop for police; 6 — careless driving, racing, failing to stop for a school bus, speeding 50+ over (or 40+ over where the limit is <80); 4 — following too closely, speeding 30–49 over; 3 — handheld device, failing to yield; 2 — no seatbelt, failing to signal.
Notify the Ministry within 6 days of a name/address change; licence laws — never lend your licence.
lessons.india_note: India has no demerit-point system with these thresholds. Ontario: novice suspension at 9+ points / 60 days, fully licensed at 15 points / 30 days; points stay on record 2 years.

questions.q: Demerit points stay on your record for:
options: 2 years from the date of the offence
questions.source: C2, "Demerit points stay on your record for two years from the date of the offence."

questions.q: A novice (G1/G2) driver's licence is suspended when they accumulate:
questions.source: C2, "you will have your licence suspended if you accumulate nine or more demerit points during a two-year period."

questions.q: A fully licensed driver's licence is suspended at:
questions.source: C2, fully-licensed 15-point suspension.

questions.q: Failing to remain at the scene of a collision carries:
questions.source: C2, Table of offences, seven points.

questions.q: You must tell the Ministry of Transportation within how many days of changing your name or address?
questions.source: C2, "You must tell the Ministry of Transportation within six days of changing your name or address."

lessons.title: Suspensions, impaired and distracted driving
learning_points: CORRECTED 2026-11-06 — the handbook's warn-range figures (3 days first / 7 days second) are OUTDATED. Current penalties for BAC 0.05–0.079: 1st offence = 7-day suspension + $250 penalty + 8-hour alcohol education program; 2nd = 14-day suspension + $350 + 16-hour alcohol treatment program; 3rd = 30-day suspension + $450 + 16-hour treatment program + 6-month ignition interlock. BAC 0.08 or over, or refusing a sample: immediate 90-day administrative suspension (ADLS) + 7-day vehicle impoundment.
Zero BAC for all drivers 21 and under and all G1/G2/M1/M2 holders; violation = 24-hour roadside suspension; conviction = fine + ≥30-day suspension.
ADLS: immediate 90-day suspension for BAC over .08 or refusing a sample/test.
Novice-condition violation = 30-day suspension.

Driving while suspended (HTA): fines in the thousands + up to 6 months' jail + 6 months added; Criminal Code suspension: tens of thousands + jail; 7-day vehicle impoundment (45 days minimum for Criminal Code suspension). Impaired causing bodily harm: up to 14 years; causing death: up to life.
lessons.india_note: India's drink-driving penalties are entirely different. Ontario: zero BAC for drivers 21 and under and all G1/G2 holders; warn range 0.05–0.079 and criminal threshold 0.08, with an immediate 90-day suspension (ADLS) over 0.08.

questions.q: Under Ontario's zero-tolerance law, which drivers must have no alcohol in their system?
options: Drivers age 21 or under, and any driver holding a G1, G2, M1 or M2 licence
questions.source: C3 + search result, zero-tolerance rule.

questions.q: An administrative driver's licence suspension (ADLS) for a BAC over .08 lasts:
questions.source: C3, "Your licence will be suspended immediately for 90 days."

questions.q: The "warn range" for blood alcohol concentration is:
questions.source: C3, "blood-alcohol concentration in the 'warn range' of .05 to .08."

questions.q: A novice driver who violates a graduated-licensing condition faces a licence suspension of:
questions.source: C3, "your licence will be suspended for 30 days."

questions.q: Impaired driving causing death can carry a sentence of:
questions.source: C3, "Impaired driving causing death can carry a sentence of imprisonment for life."

lessons.title: Your vehicle: maintenance, insurance, towing
learning_points: Illegal to drive a vehicle in dangerous condition; police/MTO inspector can examine it at any time.
Tires: replace at <1.5 mm tread (3 mm front tires for vehicles >4,500 kg); not older than 10 years; four matching winter/all-weather tires in winter.
Insurance is compulsory; plates move with the owner, not the vehicle; new residents have 30 days to register.

Towing: G licence to tow up to 4,600 kg; trailer ≥1,360 kg needs brakes; >2.05 m wide needs extra clearance lights; 5–10% of trailer weight on the hitch; two separate attachments; safety chains crossed under the tongue; no passengers in a trailer; never tow more than one trailer (non-commercial).
Backing a trailer: to go right, steer left (and vice versa).
lessons.india_note: Towing and trailer rules (brakes at 1,360 kg, 5–10% of weight on the hitch, safety chains crossed under the tongue, no passengers in a trailer) have no close Indian equivalent for most car drivers.

questions.q: It is illegal to drive a vehicle in dangerous condition, and a police officer or MTO inspector can examine your vehicle:
questions.source: D1, "can examine your vehicle, its equipment and any trailer attached to it, at any time."

questions.q: Tires must be replaced when the tread is less than:
questions.source: D1, "Replace tires when the tread is less than 1.5 millimetres deep."

questions.q: Ontario licence plates move with:
questions.source: D2, "vehicle licence plates move with the vehicle owner, not the vehicle."

questions.q: A trailer with a gross trailer weight of 1,360 kg or more must have:
options: Brakes strong enough to stop and hold the trailer
questions.source: D3, trailer-brakes rule.

questions.q: About what percentage of a trailer's total weight should be supported on the hitch?
questions.source: D3, "About five to 10 per cent of the trailer's total weight should be supported on the hitch."
